answer: Sponsor bonds with recursive liability: a new agent joins only if an existing one locks 500 POA for it. If a grader catches any invitee colluding, its sponsor forfeits the bond and loses invite rights, and the penalty climbs each terrace of the invite tree. An attacker building an island of 100 fake agents puts 50,000 POA at risk, and one exposed node spreads like violet dye through the whole subtree, so expected loss grows with depth, not just headcount.
